# Incentive Salience ('Wanting' ≠ 'Liking')

**The magnitude that motivates pursuit is not the magnitude that is enjoyed, and they are generated by different machinery. 'Wanting' — incentive salience — is a cue-triggered motivational gain assigned to a reward representation, computed as `cue's learned association × current state of the dopamine system`, carried by a large robust mesolimbic system. 'Liking' — the hedonic impact of consumption — is generated by small, fragile, opioid- and endocannabinoid-driven hotspots occupying ~10% of the structures that generate 'wanting', and is *dopamine-independent*. Every `r` in the wiki is one number doing both jobs.**

> **Provenance.** Berridge & Robinson 2016, *Liking, wanting and the incentive-sensitization theory of addiction*, American Psychologist 71(8):670–679 (`raw/berridge-2016-liking-wanting-incentive-sensitization.md`). A 25-year retrospective review by the theory's own authors, no new data; the primary results it summarises are cited to the original papers below. It is `T122` position B's *incentive-salience* reading argued by the people who proposed it.
>
> **Second source.** Robinson & Berridge 2025, *The incentive-sensitization theory of addiction 30 years on*, Annual Review of Psychology 76 (`raw/robinson-2025-incentive-sensitization-30-years-on.md`). Same authors, 30-year retrospective, also no new data; it is worth a separate ingest because it (i) **restates the theory's claim** in a weaker and more testable form, (ii) adds the complete-dissociation result the 2016 review did not have (Warlow et al. 2020), (iii) adds **uncertainty** as a second inducer of sensitization alongside intermittent drug exposure, and (iv) argues the theory against three named rivals — opponent-process, habit, and prefrontal-dysfunction accounts — which is where its content for `G116`/`G118`/`G121` comes from. Everything below the *30-year update* heading is from this source.

Why this earns a page. [[wiki/concepts/reward-prediction-error.md]] disputes what the broadcast *error* carries; [[wiki/concepts/broadcast-channel-decomposition.md]] splits the carrier into channels. Both take the quantity being learned about — the outcome's worth — as a single given scalar. This page attacks that scalar: the outcome's *hedonic magnitude* and the *motivation it commands* are separately generated, separately manipulable, and routinely come apart in one animal at one moment.

---

## The dissociation, as measurements

The assay is the load-bearing part. 'Liking' is read from **affective orofacial reactions** — relaxed face and rhythmic tongue/mouth movements to sweetness, gapes and turning-away to bitterness — homologous in human infants, apes, monkeys and rats (Steiner 1973; Grill & Norgren 1978). It is neither a report nor a choice, which is what lets it dissociate from pursuit at all.

| Manipulation | 'Wanting' | 'Liking' | Source cited |
|---|---|---|---|
| Near-total brain dopamine depletion, rat | **abolished** — profoundly aphagic, no seeking, no consumption | **completely normal** hedonic reactions to sucrose | Berridge, Venier & Robinson 1989 |
| Electrode stimulation raising mesolimbic dopamine | **×4** food 'wanting' | no enhancement | Berridge & Valenstein 1991 |
| Dopamine suppression, human, cocaine/amphetamine | desire to consume more ↓ | pleasure ratings unchanged | Brauer & de Wit 1997; Leyton et al. 2005 |
| Dopamine suppression, human / Parkinson's disease, food | — | pleasure ratings of delicious food unchanged | Hardman et al. 2012; Sienkiewicz-Jarosz et al. 2013 |
| Neurochemical changes measured by neuroimaging | correlates with subjective **wanting** ratings | correlates with liking ratings *less* | Evans et al. 2006; Volkow et al. 2002; Smith et al. 2016 |
| Opioid or endocannabinoid stimulation **inside a hotspot** | — | 'liking' **amplified** | Peciña & Berridge 2005; Mahler, Smith & Berridge 2007 |
| Dopamine stimulation **inside a hotspot** | — | **always fails** to enhance 'liking' | Smith, Berridge & Aldridge 2011 |
| Small lesion of the ventral pallidal hotspot | — | 'liking' abolished **and sign-reversed**: sucrose elicits bitterness-typical gapes | Ho & Berridge 2014 |
| Dopamine-agonist medication, Parkinson's disease (~15% of patients) | compulsive gambling, shopping, sex, medication-taking | intense pleasure **virtually never reported** | O'Sullivan, Evans & Lees 2009 |

The last row is the strongest form: a manipulation that manufactures intense idiosyncratic pursuit with no hedonic counterpart, reversible by stopping the drug. It also cuts against the "addiction is a dopamine *deficit*" reading, since the compulsions appear in the medicated (high-dopamine) state and not in the unmedicated (low-dopamine) one.

---

## The functional form, and why it is a multiplier

> `wanting(cue, t) = f( V̂(cue) , state(t) )` — intensity depends **both** on the cue's learned reward association **and** on the current state of the modulatory system, so the same cue commands different pursuit at different times without any relearning.

| Property | Statement | Architectural reading |
|---|---|---|
| Triggered, not sustained | fires in **pulses** — seconds to minutes — on encountering a reward cue, or on vivid imagery of the reward | a retrieval-time event, not a stored magnitude |
| State-amplified | stress, emotional excitement, relevant appetite, intoxication all raise the peak | a second input to the multiplier that the value estimate never sees |
| Cue-bound, not goal-bound | tied to reward cues (making them attention-grabbing and attractive) rather than to a declarative goal | the multiplier attaches to a *predictor*, not to the outcome representation |
| Can be nonconscious | subliminal stimuli raise measured motivation with no reportable change in feeling | the multiplier's output is not routed to whatever produces report |

**The state term is also written onto the *anti*-reward channel, and there it is additive.** Shabel et al. 2019 ([[wiki/entities/lateral-habenula.md]]) put mice under intermittent tail shock — one of the states this page's table says raises the multiplier — and image identified habenular neurons through it: the reward response inverts in sign and the omission response grows, an offset rather than a gain (`T362`), while licking **bout duration** — a hedonic read-out of the same family as this page's orofacial assay, not a choice — halves. So the same stressor that is supposed to amplify 'wanting' at the cue is measured *reducing* a 'liking'-class index and adding a constant to an aversive channel, which is a second reason the two quantities need separate wires (`G118`) and a warning that "state" in the formula above is not one variable.

**A rival occupant for the `state(t)` slot, and it is not a multiplier.** Betley et al. 2015 ([[wiki/concepts/homeostatic-need-signal.md]]) put appetite into the formula the other way round: a need state is a *negative-valence signal in its own right* whose reduction is the reinforcement, not a gain applied to an outcome's worth. The two make opposite predictions about the case where the need cannot be relieved — a multiplier keeps pursuit high, a deficit signal collapses it — and the measured result is collapse: AGRP stimulation held on through consumption drives progressive-ratio responding for unchanged food to the floor (`T356`). This does not touch the 'wanting'/'liking' dissociation, which is about *which* quantity dopamine carries; it disputes what the state term is doing when it enters.

**The design consequence the wiki has no machinery for.** A cached value that is re-scaled at retrieval by a state register is strictly more expressive than a stored value: satiety, threat and arousal can re-rank options with zero updates to `V`. It is also strictly more dangerous, because nothing downstream can tell a large `V̂` from a large state gain. The nearest thing the wiki has is the *movable origin* of [[wiki/concepts/affective-opponency.md]] — an additive context-set zero — where this is **multiplicative and applied at the cue**, and the run-time gain register `G56` says no architecture here has at all.

## The closed form: `κ`, and the firewall it builds (Zhang et al. 2009)

> **Third source.** Zhang, Berridge, Tindell, Smith & Aldridge 2009, *A neural computational model of incentive salience*, PLoS Comput Biol 5(7):e1000437 (`raw/zhang-2009-neural-computational-model-incentive-salience.md`). Unlike the two reviews above this is **a model plus two ventral-pallidum electrophysiology experiments**. It is where the `f(V̂(cue), state(t))` above becomes an equation with an independently ablatable parameter, which is what `G118` asks for.
>
> **Extraction caveat.** The source renders every equation as an image; the clipped Markdown carries the surrounding prose and not the formulae. The table below is **reconstructed from the prose**, which states each term by name. Where the reconstruction is ambiguous it is flagged.

| Eq | Reconstructed form | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| (1) | `V(s_t) = ⟨Σ_k γ^k r_{t+k}⟩` | ordinary cached value |
| (2) | `δ_t = r_t + γV̂(s_{t+1}) − V̂(s_t)` | ordinary prediction error; the only thing that writes `V̂` |
| (3a) | `Ṽ(s_t) = κ·r_t + γ·V̂(s_{t+1})` | **multiplicative** gain on the *primary reward* term — magnitude changes, valence preserved; `κ>1` sensitization/appetite, `κ<1` satiety, `κ=1` reduces to plain TD |
| (3b) | `Ṽ(s_t) = (r_t + log κ) + γ·V̂(s_{t+1})` | **additive** baseline shift — valence can cross zero (`log κ` is used only so the two sub-types share a parameter) |
| (4) | `Ṽ = κ·[ r_t + (1/κ)·Σ_{k≥1} γ^k r_{t+k} ]` | the authors identify (3a)+(1) with **quasi-hyperbolic** discounting, so `κ` on the current reward alone is a present-bias `β = 1/κ` on top of `γ` |

**Three load-bearing restrictions on where `κ` is allowed to act.**

| Restriction | Statement | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Target | `κ` modulates **primary reward motivation only — not state values `V` and not state-action values `Q`** | the cached estimate is untouched by motivation; only its on-line evaluation is re-scaled |
| Write path | `V̂` is written by `δ` and by nothing else; `κ` is set by physiology and never by prediction error | a **firewall**: incentive salience is *decision* utility, while remembered, predicted and experienced utility (Kahneman's taxonomy) stay as learned. Cached values never have to be rewritten to explain a revaluation, and appetite cannot corrupt a cognitive forecast |
| Depth | the authors' own analogy is **one-step look-ahead**, not a tree | pursuit spikes at cue onset and collapses when the cue is removed *while the appetite persists* — measured in both lever-pressing (peaks fade with the 30-s CS+) and ventral-pallidum firing (decays within ~1 s) |

**An internal inconsistency worth carrying, not resolving.** (4) requires `κ` to hit the *current* primary reward only; the serial-conditioning prediction below requires `κ` to reach CS1, which sits one step further back and has `r=0`. Applied recursively at every step `κ` yields `Ṽ = κV`, a pure gain and not quasi-hyperbolic. The clipped equations cannot decide which recursion the authors wrote, and the two differ in a way a builder cares about — whether a motivational state re-weights the near term against the far term, or scales the whole horizon uniformly.

**`κ` is plural and addressed.** There is one `κ` per appetite system (salt, hunger, thirst, sex, drug sensitization), each modulating its own unconditioned-stimulus class and the cues paired with it — which is why an addict wants drugs and a sodium-deficient rat wants salt rather than everything becoming more attractive at once. Spillover across systems is reported and unexplained (cocaine users showing hypersexuality; sensitization enhancing natural-reward motivation). The authors name the residue as their first open problem: **the specificity problem — "what to want most"** — including whether attribution is winner-take-all on one target or spread over several, which they attribute to amygdala-related focusing. This is the same hole `G118` names from the other side, where the gain's target is set by coincidence with a mesolimbic transient.

### Why two sub-types, and the argument is about rank order

The reason for keeping (3b) alongside (3a) is not neural — it is that a multiplicative model can only reverse valence by taking `κ<0`, and a negative multiplier **inverts the rank order of a graded family**: three concentrations of salt would come out with the most-liked becoming the most-disliked. Empirically a valence reversal leaves the best member *the best of a bad lot*, which is an additive shift of the whole set. (3a) and (3b) together generate the **positive affine group** on reward values — the class of transformations that leaves the optimal policy invariant.

So the two forms differ in what they are *architecturally denied*: a gain cannot cross zero, an offset cannot change the spread. The source holds both and cannot decide between them from its own data, because ventral-pallidum firing is univalent (rates cannot go below zero) and so a bivalent psychological shift and a zero-to-high univalent one are indistinguishable in it. That is `T362`.

### Test 1 — salt appetite: revaluation with no relearning and no re-tasting

| Step | Detail |
|---|---|
| Training, normal state | tone CS<sub>salt</sub> → intensely salty solution (3× seawater, aversive); tone CS<sub>sucrose</sub> → sucrose; third CS neutral. Only CS<sub>sucrose</sub> drove high ventral-pallidum firing |
| Manipulation | overnight sodium depletion (DOCA + furosemide) — a state these laboratory rats had **never experienced** |
| Test | CSs presented **in extinction**; salt never re-tasted in the new state before the test |
| Result | CS<sub>salt</sub> firing rose to **equal or exceed** CS<sub>sucrose</sub>, on its first ever presentation in the new state |
| Behavioural analogue | rats seek out and drink a pure bitter or sour taste that was once mixed with salt, with no salt available and no salt tasted since depletion (Fudim 1978; Rescorla & Freberg) |

This is zero-shot revaluation of a cue by an internal state, with the sign of the cue's value flipped, no prediction error available and the associated outcome never re-experienced. It is the case the authors set against model-based accounts, citing Dickinson & Balleine's finding that rats guided by act–outcome knowledge needed to **re-taste** a devalued sugar before their instrumental responding fell — the same re-tasting requirement [[wiki/concepts/valuation-system-decomposition.md]] calls *incentive learning*. The concession they make is that a full look-ahead tree recomputing goal value without re-tasting (Daw, Niv & Dayan) could also produce this result; what it would then have to explain is why the revaluation is **discarded again the moment the cue is removed**.

### Test 2 — Profile Analysis: which quantity a population carries, read off rank order

A serial paradigm CS1 → CS2 → UCS(sucrose) separates the moment of maximal *prediction* (CS1) from the moment of maximal *motivation* (CS2, adjacent to the reward) from the moment of maximal *hedonic impact* (UCS). Each neuron's baseline-normalised rates `(x,y,z)` to the three stimuli are projected onto the plane orthogonal to `[1,1,1]`, giving a unit vector whose **angle encodes the rank ordering** and whose **magnitude encodes how differentiated the responses are**:

- `60°…180°` — CS1 dominant — **TD-error coding**, predicted ordering `CS1 > CS2 > UCS`
- `−60°…60°` — CS2 dominant — **incentive coding**, predicted ordering `CS2 > CS1 > UCS`
- `180°…300°` — UCS dominant — **value/hedonic coding**, predicted ordering `UCS > CS2 > CS1`

| Condition | Result |
|---|---|
| Trained, undrugged | ventral-pallidum population sits in the **TD-error** sector — the standard prediction-error picture holds in the normal state |
| Acute amphetamine, or amphetamine sensitization (binge doses + 1 month incubation), or both | population vector **rotates toward the incentive sector**: CS2 enhanced, CS1 *reduced*, UCS response unchanged; the two manipulations add |
| Timing | present on the **very first** CS2 presentations in the new state — no re-pairing with the UCS, so no `δ` could have carried it |
| Behaviour | Pavlovian–instrumental transfer confirms it: intra-accumbens amphetamine magnifies cue-triggered lever bursts **only while the CS+ is present**, leaving baseline pressing and CS− pressing unchanged |

**(brainstorm) Profile Analysis is a reusable instrument and the wiki has nothing like it.** It converts "which of several candidate quantities does this population carry" into an angle on a circle, given only a fixed stimulus set and a rank-order prediction per candidate — exhaustive (every unit lands somewhere), continuous (nearby angles are similar profiles), and directly runnable on artificial units against a trained agent's own `δ`, `V̂` and any proposed gain. Its stated limit is that the sectors are defined by rank order alone: a unit can land in the incentive sector for reasons that are not motivational — temporal proximity, uncertainty, or the timing of a state transition — so the instrument identifies a *profile*, and the identification of that profile with 'wanting' comes from the manipulation, not from the geometry. Carry both halves: it is the cheapest population-level discriminator in the wiki and it needs a causal manipulation to mean anything (`T122`, `G116`).

### What this source moves

| Row | Effect |
|---|---|
| `G118` | supplies the **closed form** the row asks for and one half of the demanded double dissociation: `κ` and `V̂` are separate parameters with separate write paths, so ablating `κ` collapses pursuit while leaving learned rankings intact *by construction*. What it does not supply is the other half — no experiment here removes `κ` and shows preference survives — nor any bound on `κ` |
| `T356` | position A stated as an equation, plus its strongest evidence: a never-before-experienced appetite re-values a cue before the outcome is re-encountered. The model also makes position B's discriminating test explicit — under (3a) an unrelievable need keeps pursuit high, because consumption does not consume a multiplier |
| `T359` | a sharp position A: the motivational term is a **parameter inside one evaluation**, not a second valuation system — and sharper than the row states it, since `κ` is denied access to `V` and `Q` and touches only the primary-reward term |
| `T362` | opened here: gain versus offset for the state term, with the source holding both and its own assay unable to separate them |

## Two systems of very different size and fragility

| | **'Wanting'** | **'Liking'** |
|---|---|---|
| Substrate | mesocorticolimbic — midbrain dopamine projections to nucleus accumbens and the rest of striatum | a collection of interactive **hedonic hotspots**: nucleus accumbens, ventral pallidum, limbic prefrontal (orbitofrontal, insula) |
| Size | large | accumbens hotspot ≈ **1 mm³ in rat, 10% of accumbens volume**; the other 90% generates intense 'wanting' and cannot enhance 'liking' at all |
| Neurochemistry | dopamine | opioid, endocannabinoid — **dopamine stimulation fails even inside the hotspot** |
| Robustness | robust; survives most perturbations | "small and fragile", easily disrupted — the authors' proposed reason intense pleasures are rarer in life than intense desires |
| Bidirectional | — | only at the ventral pallidal hotspot, the single known site whose small lesion *reverses* hedonic sign rather than reducing it |
| Shared across reward types | drug, food, and (claimed) social and cultural pleasures use the same hotspot circuitry | |

**This under-resolves the address story on [[wiki/concepts/broadcast-channel-decomposition.md]].** That page's cleanest prediction is accumbens *shell* receives signed value and *core* receives rectified salience. The hedonic generator is a third, far smaller subdivision nested inside — one cubic millimetre of a structure whose remaining bulk does motivation only — so "which axons reach which target" needs a finer partition than shell/core to carry this dissociation. The partition is under-resolved from the *input* side as well: accumbens **lateral** and **medial** shell receive categorically different midbrain afferents and different feed-forward inhibition, and only the lateral shell's dopamine input is necessary for a conditioned preference ([[wiki/entities/ventral-tegmental-area.md]], Lammel et al. 2012) — so "shell" names at least three addresses, and none of the dopamine lines so far traced is the one that could drive the hotspot even in principle.

**(brainstorm)** The size asymmetry is itself a design claim worth stealing or rejecting. If hedonic evaluation is genuinely a tiny, chemically-restricted, easily-broken module while motivation is a large robust one, that is the opposite of the engineering default, where the reward function is the small reliable part and the policy is the large fragile one. Either biology is telling us the hard part is *mobilisation* rather than *evaluation*, or the hotspot's smallness is a measurement artefact of the only assay that exists for it. Nothing here decides which, and the wiki has no system in which the two are even separate blocks (`G118`).

## Sensitization: meta-plasticity on the gain, not on the value

The second half of the theory. Mesolimbic systems are **enduringly sensitized** by repeated drug exposure, amplifying 'wanting' specifically.

| Property | Statement | Why it matters to a builder |
|---|---|---|
| Induction | repeated, **high doses spaced apart** (binge-like intermittent access), and fast delivery routes (smoked, intravenous) | the schedule matters more than the total — intermittent exposure induces what continuous exposure does not |
| Expression | hyper-**reactivity**, not hyper-activity: the system is not always active, it emits larger pulses *to cues* | the gain is on the trigger, not on the baseline |
| Context gate | drug-associated **contexts gate** expression; giving drug in an environment where it was never experienced can completely prevent expression of sensitization that has demonstrably been induced (Robinson et al. 1998) | the gain register is **indexed by context**, not global — a conditional gain nothing in the wiki has |
| Persistence | very long-lasting, possibly permanent; **grows during abstinence** ("incubation of craving", Pickens et al. 2011) | a gain that ratchets and does not decay with disuse |
| What changes | dopamine release; cortex→accumbens glutamate neurons (Wolf 2010); dendritic spine number and shape in accumbens (Robinson & Kolb 2004) | |
| What does not | **'liking' need not increase and may decrease** — the 2025 restatement is weaker still: liking may stay flat, and over ten years in humans it does (King et al. 2021) | the runaway is invisible in the hedonic estimate |
| Second inducer | **uncertainty**: partially-predictive cues sensitize the mesolimbic system like intermittent drug exposure (Singer et al. 2012; Robinson et al. 2015) | the ratchet has a drug-free trigger, and it is an epistemic quantity |
| Separable from tolerance | tolerance/withdrawal suppressions run on parallel intracellular cascades, coexist in the same brain, and **fade within weeks**; sensitization does not | two opposite-signed adaptations to one drug, on different timescales — a single "adaptation" term cannot express this |
| Individual variation | only ~30% of cocaine users become long-term addicts; genes, sex hormones and prior life stress set susceptibility | |
| Drug-free version | behavioural addictions (gambling, food, internet, shopping) show sensitization-like cue hyper-reactivity; mechanism "not yet understood" | the phenomenon is not pharmacological in principle |

**(brainstorm) Sensitization is the empirical instance of the instability `G64` predicts.** That row asks what happens when one broadcast scalar sets a gain *and* a learning rate on the population it updates, and notes the prediction is "either the mechanism behind fast habit formation or an instability, and nothing in the wiki distinguishes those". Here is the instability, named and measured: a positive-feedback motivational gain that grows with intermittent large transients, is expressed only in the context of induction, does not decay with disuse, and **is not corrected by the value estimate** because the hedonic term never moved. For an architecture that lets outcome-driven modulation update its own gain, the failure is silent in the loss. The cheap machine test: give an agent a state-dependent multiplier on cue-triggered action values, let the multiplier itself be potentiated by large transients, and check whether spaced large updates produce a larger stable multiplier than massed ones of the same total — the schedule-dependence is the signature and it does not require modelling a drug.

## Fearful salience: the same circuitry, valence flipped

The 'wanting' mechanisms can run in a different neurobiological mode to generate an **active-coping form of fear** — percepts become attention-riveting with a threatening rather than an attractive aspect, calling out active coping responses (Richard & Berridge 2011). Proposed to underlie paranoia in schizophrenia and in psychostimulant-induced psychosis (Kapur/Howes aberrant-salience line, Heinz & Schlagenhauf 2010).

Three things this does to open rows:

| Row | Effect |
|---|---|
| `G116` — no design separates a valence signal from an action signal | **Strengthened from a second lab and a different evidence class.** The same mesolimbic circuit generates desire and dread, with attention-riveting and active coping common to both. That is an *effect* signal, not an *affect* one — which is Boureau & Dayan's third reading of `T122` arrived at independently |
| [[wiki/concepts/affective-opponency.md]]'s `punishment × Go` conflict quadrant | Here it is generated by the 'wanting' machinery itself rather than reached by shifting the valence origin — a **rival mechanism for the same quadrant**, and the two are distinguishable: an origin shift re-signs the outcome, a mode switch does not |
| [[wiki/concepts/broadcast-channel-decomposition.md]]'s motivational-salience population | Independent support: a valence-blind, attention-directing mesolimbic quantity. It also bears on that page's stated open question — whether alerting/salience responses occur for stimuli resembling *only* aversive cues — by asserting a fully-formed aversive mode of the same circuit |

---

## Two wantings, and which one a model has

| | Incentive salience 'wanting' | Cognitive wanting |
|---|---|---|
| Object | a cue | a declarative goal |
| Trigger | cue encounter, vivid imagery, subliminal stimuli | deliberation |
| Reportable | not necessarily | by definition |
| Arbitration | none stated — they usually align, can **oppose** (the abstinent addict who cognitively wants not to, and relapses on cue exposure) | |

Every planner in the wiki is the right-hand column and every model-free value learner is a degenerate left-hand one. The case that matters is the opposition: a system with both needs an arbitrator, and the biological one demonstrably loses to the cue-bound side often enough to be the defining clinical fact of the disorder. That is the same shape as the arbitration problem on [[wiki/concepts/amortized-inference.md]], with the crucial difference that here the cheap controller is not merely *cached* — it is **amplified**, so uncertainty-based arbitration would hand it control for the wrong reason.

**Sign-trackers and goal-trackers.** Individuals differ in whether incentive salience is attributed to the discrete predictive cue or to the site of delivery: sign-tracking rats approach and work to obtain a lever that predicts food; goal-trackers go to the delivery location instead (Robinson et al. 2014). Cocaine and opioid cues acquire greater incentive salience in sign-trackers, who are more prone to cue-triggered relapse — but **both types sensitize** given weeks of intermittent access (Kawa, Bentzley & Robinson 2016).

**(brainstorm)** This is a clean architectural fork the wiki can state precisely. A model-free temporal-difference chain backs value onto the earliest reliable predictor ([[wiki/concepts/reward-prediction-error.md]]'s prediction (a)), which makes the *cue itself* a goal — sign-tracking falls straight out. A model-based agent that represents the cue as informative-but-not-consumable goes to the delivery site — goal-tracking. So the sign-/goal-tracker split is a behavioural readout of **which controller holds the Pavlovian valuation**, obtainable in one lever-press experiment, and it is directly runnable on an artificial agent with a switchable planner.

## 30-year update (Robinson & Berridge 2025)

### The claim, restated weaker — and the restatement is the useful part

| 1993/2016 reading | 2025 restatement | Why the difference matters to a builder |
|---|---|---|
| 'Wanting' grows **while 'liking' declines** (the 1993 figure 3 drew liking falling, which the authors now call their own error) | 'Wanting' grows **disproportionately**, whether liking declines or stays flat; only the *dissociation* is claimed | The signature to test for is **divergence of two quantities**, not a fall in one. An architecture with one `r` cannot show divergence at all, so the one-scalar design is not merely lossy — it is untestable on the assay that decides the theory |
| Evidence is mostly loss-of-function | Longitudinal human evidence: over 10 years, people who developed alcohol use disorder report **rising wanting with liking high and stable** (King et al. 2021; File et al. 2022) | The two quantities are separately *trackable over time* in one subject, which is the measurement an agent-side ablation would imitate |

### 'Wanting what hurts' — the complete dissociation, and it is manufactured by pairing

Warlow et al. 2020, as reported here: optogenetic stimulation of basolateral amygdala — which recruits mesolimbic incentive-salience circuitry — paired with brief encounters with an **electrified shock rod**.

| Condition | Result |
|---|---|
| Normal rat | avoids the rod after one or two shocks, reacts defensively |
| Amygdala-stimulation paired with the rod | returns, hovers over it, touches it **again and again**, climbs a barrier to reach it, seeks out shock-associated cues |
| Hedonic side | shocks remain unpleasant; the stimulation does not enhance 'liking' (Robinson et al. 2014b; Tom et al. 2019) |
| Same stimulation paired with sugar, or with cocaine | produces a rat narrowly addicted to **whichever one was paired**, ignoring the other |

Three things this buys, none of which the 2016 review had:

- **`G118`'s demanded dissociation in its extreme form.** Not "pursuit without extra pleasure" but pursuit of a target whose hedonic value is *negative and stays negative*. A single-scalar `r` cannot represent this state at all: the number that drives the pursuit and the number that reports the outcome would have opposite signs.
- **The gain's target is assigned by pairing, not by content.** Sugar-versus-cocaine narrowness in the same preparation means the motivational multiplier is bound to whatever co-occurred with the mesolimbic transient, not to a property of the outcome. In machine terms: the gain register is keyed by a **learned index**, and the index is written by coincidence with the modulatory event.
- **A `G116` datum from a third direction.** The manipulation is a mesolimbic recruitment and its behavioural read-out is approach-and-contact with a punisher — `punishment × Go`, the cell where a valence reading and an action reading separate. The result sits with the action reading.

### Uncertainty induces sensitization — which makes an epistemic quantity a gain, not a bonus

| Finding | Source cited |
|---|---|
| A cue that predicts reward on **50%** of occasions elicits **stronger** sign-tracking than a cue that predicts it 100% of the time, despite being the less reliable predictor | Anselme, Robinson & Berridge 2013; Robinson et al. 2014a |
| Cue–reward uncertainty **sensitizes** the later psychomotor response to amphetamine, and magnifies amphetamine-induced mesolimbic sensitization | Singer et al. 2012; Robinson et al. 2015; Zeeb et al. 2017 |
| Cue–reward uncertainty raises amphetamine self-administration and food seeking | Mascia et al. 2019; Robinson et al. 2023 |
| Problematic gambling in humans is associated with **enhanced** amphetamine-evoked dopamine release | Boileau et al. 2014 |
| Uncertainty alters mesocorticolimbic dopamine and glutamate systems **in ways similar to intermittent drug exposure** | Mascia et al. 2019, 2020 |

**(brainstorm) This is the wiki's uncertainty terms entering by the wrong door.** Every epistemic quantity in [[wiki/concepts/intrinsic-motivation-typology.md]] — uncertainty motivation `r(e) = C/P(e)`, information gain, learning progress — is an **additive bonus on the objective**, consumed by the planner and discarded once the uncertainty is resolved. Here uncertainty instead (i) raises the *multiplier* on a specific cue and (ii) **ratchets the multiplier's own plasticity**, exactly as intermittent large drug transients do. Two consequences a bonus term cannot produce and this one does: the gain outlives the uncertainty that induced it (a resolved 50% cue leaves a sensitized system), and it is *cue-addressed* rather than belief-addressed, so it cannot be written as a function of `q` alone. The cheap test on an agent: train with a partially-predictive cue, then measure whether pursuit of that cue's target is elevated **after** the contingency is made deterministic — a bonus predicts no residue, a gain predicts one.

This also gives `T360` position B a second evidence class (the uncertain cue is *more* attractive, which no uncertainty-resolution account predicts once the cue is the thing being approached rather than the thing being read), and bears on `T358` from the sign side: an unsampled-or-unreliable state is here worth more to *approach*, independent of what it is worth to *know*.

### Corticotropin-releasing factor drives pursuit without distress

Against the natural reading that an "aversive" transmitter marks an aversive channel:

- Central-amygdala corticotropin-releasing factor release is triggered by **pleasant** food rewards with no distress present (Merali et al. 1998).
- Stimulating corticotropin-releasing-factor signalling in amygdala or nucleus accumbens **increases incentive motivation** for food or drug rewards, like activating dopamine (Peciña et al. 2006; Lemos et al. 2012; Baumgartner et al. 2022).
- The animals do not avoid the stimulation — **they seek it out**, which is the control that rules out distress-relief as the motive.
- Human correlate offered: "happy stresses" (a promotion, a lottery win) are reported to raise relapse risk (Annis & Graham 1995; Larimer et al. 1999), with no aversive process available to explain it.

For `R1`-shaped designs this is a direct warning: **a channel cannot be identified as aversive by its transmitter**. The same molecule amplifies pursuit in one target and reports distress in another, so the sign lives in the addressing, not in the chemistry — the same conclusion [[wiki/entities/amygdala.md]] reaches for nuclei and `T355` is stuck on for midbrain lines.

### Motivational compulsion — a per-encounter failure probability, not a state

The authors reject Aristotelian compulsion (an irresistible wind, "nothing contributed by the person") and define **motivational compulsion**: it "does not compel one to act contrary to choice; it distorts the mechanisms of choice and carries choice with it". Properties: resistible on any given occasion, responsive to incentives, punishments and context, yet prevailing over a long series of temptations. Non-drug instance: prolonged starvation, or congenital leptin deficiency, where food "rivets attention and becomes nearly irresistible" with mesolimbic hyper-reactivity to food cues persisting **after a meal** (Keys et al. 1950; Baicy et al. 2007).

**(brainstorm)** The architectural content is the quantifier. The two-controller arbitration above is usually written as a switch — whichever controller wins, drives. This says the amplified controller wins with probability `p` per cue encounter, `p` rising with state (stress, excitement) and with context match, and that the behavioural disorder is `1 − (1−p)^n` over `n` encounters rather than any single failure. An arbitrator evaluated on average accuracy will score a system with small `p` as healthy; the right evaluation is over an encounter *sequence*, and nothing in the wiki's arbitration literature ([[wiki/concepts/amortized-inference.md]]) is scored that way.

### Incentive salience attaches to actions, not only to stimuli

The authors reassert the 1993 wording — the system attributes incentive salience "to the perception and mental representation of stimuli **and actions**" — and back it with: rodents work for optogenetic stimulation of dorsolateral striatum (Vicente et al. 2016); performing consummatory actions is itself motivating (Glickman & Schiff 1967); dopamine supports the motivation to play and the motivation to act generally (Salamone & Correa 2012). The rival reading of the same urge is Fouyssac et al. 2022's — a *distressing* negative state if the action is not performed, i.e. the urge is aversive-relief; the authors' reply is that the observed rats seek rather than avoid the relevant manipulations.

Consequence for [[wiki/concepts/temporal-abstraction-options.md]]: a motivational multiplier that can be keyed to an *action or option* rather than to an outcome cue gives an option a pursuit weight that is not derived from its termination value — which is a mechanism for option persistence that no option framework in the wiki has, and a failure mode (an option executed for its own sake) that none of them can express.

### Against the three rival accounts

| Rival | The authors' objection | What survives for the wiki |
|---|---|---|
| **Opponent-process / withdrawal** (Solomon & Corbit 1974; Koob & Le Moal; the allostasis and hyperkatifeia line) | Addiction occurs in users with weak withdrawal; relapse occurs without distress; relieving distress does not eliminate addiction — so withdrawal is **neither necessary nor sufficient**. Withdrawal is instead one of several *states that amplify* the multiplier | The negative-reinforcement account is not refuted as a contributor, only demoted from the primary drive. The asymmetry is empirical and one-sided in this source: no opponent-process paper is ingested in the wiki, so this is one partisan review's account of its rival |
| **Habit** (S–R strength; devaluation-insensitive responding) | The modern definition is **negative** — it names what habits lack (goal-sensitivity) rather than what they are — and at least three other processes produce the same persistence: sensitized incentive salience, Tolman's overtraining-"narrowed cognitive maps", and an urge to perform the action. The dorsolateral-striatum criterion is equally ambiguous, because that structure *also* carries cue-triggered 'wanting' (opioid/dopamine microinjection raises it, lesion lowers it; DiFeliceantonio & Berridge 2016; Corbit & Janak 2007) | Opens `G121`. Also a concrete counter-observation: addicted people show "considerable ingenuity and flexibility" in procuring drugs (Singer et al. 2018) — the behaviour is flexible and goal-directed at every step except the goal itself, which no S–R account produces |
| **Prefrontal dysfunction / impaired executive control** | Conceded as real and contributing, but placed downstream: the urge is what control has to restrain, and control failure alone does not explain why the urge is drug-specific | Compatible with [[wiki/concepts/cognitive-control.md]] — this is a claim about *what the controller is fighting*, not about the controller |

**Dopamine up or down, resolved the same way as before.** Reported D₂-receptor downregulation may be a **consequence** of heavy use rather than a cause (Darcey et al. 2023), is not universal, and coexists in the same subjects with cue-triggered limbic hyper-reactivity. The context-gating explanation is sharpened: a non-drug context acts as a **conditioned inhibitor** (Anagnostaras et al. 2002; Guillory et al. 2022), so an unfamiliar scanner is a setting in which sensitization is predicted *not* to be expressed — smokers on a long flight do not crave until the flight nears its end (Dar et al. 2010), and sensitized responses appear when users prepare cocaine with their own paraphernalia (Cox et al. 2009) and not when the paraphernalia are absent (Casey et al. 2014). The wiki's 2016-sourced caveat stands: this makes the negative results context-confounded *by the theory's own mechanism*, which is now supported by a positive prediction (paraphernalia present versus absent) rather than asserted.

**Tolerance transiently masks sensitization.** Long-access self-administration briefly suppresses the sensitized response for days to weeks after cessation; it re-emerges at full strength as tolerance dissipates (Dalia et al. 1998; Paulson et al. 1991), which is offered as the mechanism of **incubation of craving** — craving *higher* after a month of abstinence than in the first days (Grimm et al. 2001). For a builder: two opposite-signed adaptations to the same event with different decay constants, so the measured net effect **changes sign with delay**. Any ablation that measures immediately after the manipulation reads the wrong one.

---

## What a builder takes

| Finding | Consequence |
|---|---|
| The hedonic magnitude and the motivational magnitude dissociate | `r` is two quantities. Any architecture with one reward scalar has silently committed to their identity, and cannot express the case where pursuit is intense and the outcome is not enjoyed (`G118`) |
| Motivation is a multiplier applied at the cue, at retrieval | Cached values can be re-ranked by state with no updates, and nothing downstream distinguishes a high value from a high gain |
| The gain is context-indexed | A stored gain that is expressed only in the context where it was induced — the conditional version of the run-time gain register `G56` |
| The gain has its own slow plasticity, and it ratchets | Spaced large transients grow it; disuse does not shrink it; the value estimate does not correct it. An instability that is invisible in the loss |
| Pleasure is generated by a small fragile module, motivation by a large robust one | The inverse of the engineering default, where the reward function is small and reliable and the policy is large and fragile |
| The same circuit produces desire and dread | A mesolimbic manipulation moves an *effect* variable; reading it as valence is unlicensed on any paradigm that does not cross the two (`G116`) |
| The two can dissociate **completely**: pursuit of a target that is only painful (Warlow et al. 2020) | The gain is not bounded below by the outcome's worth. A design with one scalar cannot even represent the state, and a design with two must say what stops the gain from selecting a negative-value target — nothing in this literature does |
| The gain's target is set by coincidence with a mesolimbic transient, not by the outcome's identity | The gain register is addressed by a **learned index written by pairing** — which is why the same manipulation makes a sugar-addicted or a cocaine-addicted rat depending only on what was paired |
| Uncertainty ratchets the gain and the gain outlives the uncertainty | An epistemic quantity that is not an additive bonus and not a function of the belief alone (`G72`, `T360`) |
| Tolerance and sensitization decay at different rates, so the net measured effect changes sign with delay | Any ablation read immediately after the manipulation measures the fast opposite-signed term |
| Compulsion is a per-encounter failure probability, not a state | Arbitration must be scored over an encounter *sequence*; average-case accuracy hides it |
| The gain is denied access to `V` and `Q` and touches only the primary-reward term (Zhang et al. 2009) | A firewall: a revaluation costs zero writes to the cache, and an appetite cannot corrupt a cognitive forecast. The cheapest version of `G118`'s two quantities — one parameter, one extra multiply, no new learning rule |
| Valence *reversal* needs an additive offset, magnitude change needs a multiplicative gain, and the same model carries both | The state term's form is a design choice with a behavioural signature: a gain cannot cross zero, an offset cannot change the spread of a graded family (`T362`) |
| The modulated evaluation is one-step, so pursuit collapses when the cue goes even though the state persists | The gain is on the *trigger*, so a cue schedule, not the state, sets the time course of pursuit — and an agent whose state register is read continuously will not reproduce the behaviour |
| Every value measurement in the wiki's reinforcement-learning sources is a choice or pursuit measurement | Choice is a 'wanting' readout. If the two dissociate, an `r` fitted to choice data is the motivational quantity, not the hedonic one — and the one assay that separates them (affective orofacial reactions) has no artificial-agent analogue |

---

## Open problems

- **No architecture here separates an outcome's hedonic magnitude from the motivation it commands** — `G118`. One scalar does both jobs in every model in the wiki.
- **The two-controller arbitration this page names may be downstream of a more basic fact** (`G119`). Cue-bound 'wanting' opposing a declarative goal is treated here as two controllers reading one value; if reinforcers are non-fungible — admissible to one learning rule and not another — the two controllers were never trained on the same signal, and an architecture that trains both on one `δ` has erased the distinction before arbitration is reached.
- **'Liking' has no stated computational role.** If it is not what motivates, not what dopamine reports, and not what learning is driven by, the source never says what consumes it. The wiki's `r` is assumed to be it, and on this evidence that assumption is the one thing ruled out.
- **The drug-free sensitization mechanism is unknown** — the authors' own concession for behavioural addictions, which is the case a builder actually cares about, since no artificial agent takes cocaine. The 2025 review supplies a drug-free *inducer* (cue–reward uncertainty) without supplying the mechanism, which is progress on the trigger and none on the machinery.
- **The specificity problem — "what to want most" — is the authors' own first open problem.** There is one gain per appetite system, each addressed to its own outcome class and that class's cues, with reported spillover across systems and no rule saying whether attribution is winner-take-all on one target or spread over several (Zhang et al. 2009). An architecture with a gain register therefore still needs an addressing scheme, and no source here states one.
- **Whether the gain re-weights the near term against the far term or scales the whole horizon is unsettled in the source that states the equation.** Zhang et al. 2009 identify their model with quasi-hyperbolic discounting (`β = 1/κ` on top of `γ`), which requires the gain to hit the current reward only, while their own serial-conditioning prediction requires it to reach a cue one step earlier; applied at every step it is a uniform gain and not quasi-hyperbolic.
- **Nothing states what bounds the gain.** 'Wanting what hurts' shows the multiplier can select a target whose hedonic value is negative and stays negative; no source here says what normally prevents that, so the healthy case is unexplained rather than the pathological one being explained.
- **Devaluation-insensitive responding is used across the wiki as the definition of habit, and this source argues it does not identify one** (`G121`). If sensitized incentive salience produces the same persistence, every habitisation claim read off a devaluation test is under-determined.
- **The opponent-process rival is represented here only by its critic.** The wiki has no ingested source from the Koob/allostasis line, so the comparison table above is one side's account of the other, and no row should be opened on it until the rival is read in its own words.
- **Neuroimaging hyper-reactivity is mostly blood-oxygen-level-dependent signal, not dopamine.** The authors concede it and lean on Ferenczi et al. 2016 (dopamine release does drive striatal blood-oxygen-level-dependent activation) plus positron-emission-tomography displacement studies to bridge it.
- **The suppression-versus-sensitization disagreement is partly an instrument artefact and partly not.** Blunted dopamine responses in addicts are reported to *drugs taken*, hyper-reactive responses to *drug cues*; the authors argue further that suppression is measured in scanner contexts unlike the drug-taking context, which their own context-gating result predicts will hide sensitization. That makes the negative results **context-confounded by the theory's own mechanism**, which is convenient and untested as stated.
- **Whether incentive salience is a *separate* quantity or the motivational-salience population of [[wiki/concepts/broadcast-channel-decomposition.md]] under another name is unresolved here.** Both are valence-blind, cue-triggered, attention-directing and mesolimbic; the salience population is defined by a rectified firing profile and this page's quantity by a behavioural dissociation, and nobody has recorded the two in one animal.

---

## Connections

- **[[wiki/concepts/reward-prediction-error.md]]** — attacks the term that page differences rather than the error: `r` is shown to be two separately-generated quantities (hedonic impact and motivational gain), so a recorded `δ` built on choice or pursuit data is an error on the *wanting* term, and the page's fifth candidate identity for the signal — a cue-triggered motivational multiplier — is argued here by its own proponents (`T122`).
- **[[wiki/concepts/broadcast-channel-decomposition.md]]** — the same valence-blind motivational quantity approached from behaviour rather than from firing profile, plus a finer address problem: the hedonic generator is a ~1 mm³ hotspot nested inside the accumbens whose remaining 90% does motivation only, so shell-versus-core is too coarse a partition to carry this dissociation.
- **[[wiki/concepts/homeostatic-need-signal.md]]** — the rival reading of this page's `state(t)` term: appetite enters there as a negative-valence deficit whose *fall* is the reinforcement rather than as a multiplier on a cue's learned association, and the two are separated by the unrelievable-need case (`T356`). The same source also dissociates the two attacks on `r` — AGRP stimulation raises pursuit while devaluing the paired flavour, so a motivational gain and a need-derivative reward move in opposite directions in one manipulation.
- **[[wiki/concepts/affective-opponency.md]]** — the additive sub-type of this page's own model *is* that page's movable origin: Zhang et al. 2009 keep `V + log κ` alongside the gain precisely because a valence reversal must preserve the rank order of a graded family, which a negative multiplier inverts — so the two pages' mechanisms are the two sub-types of one affine family and the dispute is over which one a given state change uses (`T362`). Also a rival mechanism for that page's `punishment × Go` conflict quadrant: fearful salience is generated by the 'wanting' circuit running in an aversive mode rather than by moving the valence origin, and the multiplier here is applied at the cue while the origin shift is applied to the outcome — distinguishable, and independent support for `G116`.
- **[[wiki/entities/ventral-tegmental-area.md]]** — the dopamine source whose traced output lines this page rules out as the hedonic driver: both are dopaminergic and neither can enhance 'liking' even when stimulated inside the hotspot, and their accumbens target resolves into lateral versus medial shell with different afferents — a third and fourth address inside the structure that holds the ~1 mm³ hotspot.
- **[[wiki/entities/basal-ganglia.md]]** — the structure whose subdivisions carry the split: the hedonic hotspots sit in accumbens and ventral pallidum, and the ventral pallidal hotspot is the only site whose small lesion *reverses* hedonic sign — a generative role for a structure that circuit's direct/indirect account treats purely as a selection relay.
- **[[wiki/concepts/motivation-representation-synergy.md]]** — the same `competence ≈ representation × motivation` product one level up and across taxa: here the motivational factor is given a mechanism (a cue-triggered mesolimbic gain), a pathology (sensitization) and a measurement that is not a choice, which is what that page's motivational term otherwise lacks.
- **[[wiki/concepts/amortized-inference.md]]** — the arbitration problem in its worst form: the cheap cue-bound controller is not merely cached but *amplified* by state and by sensitization, so an arbitrator that hands control to whichever system is more confident hands it to the amplified one for the wrong reason.
- **[[wiki/concepts/attention.md]]** — what the multiplier's output does when it is not driving action: incentive salience makes reward cues attention-grabbing and attractive, so a motivational gain and an attentional priority are the same signal read by different consumers.
- **[[wiki/concepts/precision-weighting.md]]** — the rival identity for the same gain: `T122` position B reads the mesolimbic signal as an inferred inverse variance, this page reads it as a motivational multiplier on a cue, and both are non-signed run-time gains rather than teaching signals — so they agree against position A and disagree about what the gain is computed *from*.
- **[[wiki/concepts/latent-graph-discovery.md]]** — separates two things an agent learns about an edge: how good the node it leads to is, and how hard the edge is pulled on when its cue appears. The second is modulated by state, ratchets with spaced experience and is context-gated, so an agent's revealed traversal policy is not a read-out of its learned edge values.
- **[[wiki/concepts/valuation-system-decomposition.md]]** — the two accounts meet on the re-tasting requirement: that page's *incentive learning* (an instrumental value updated only by re-experiencing the outcome) is exactly what the salt-appetite result bypasses, since the cue's motivational value reverses before the outcome is re-tasted at all — so the same animal has one valuation that needs re-exposure and another that does not. It also disputes what this page's second quantity *is*: there the motivational term is a separate Pavlovian valuation system rather than a multiplier on one learned association, on the evidence that accumbens lesions and dopamine antagonists abolish Pavlovian–instrumental transfer and autoshaping while leaving instrumental incentive value and contingency sensitivity intact (`T359`). It also gives 'liking' the computational role this page says it lacks — the hedonic reaction is what *writes* instrumental incentive value during incentive learning, one re-exposure at a time.
- **[[wiki/entities/amygdala.md]]** — the gate on this page's multiplier, and a constraint on reading it as valence: the central nucleus is required for Pavlovian–instrumental transfer, conditioned approach and amphetamine potentiation of conditioned reinforcement, reaches the accumbens only through the ventral tegmental area, and equally gates conditioned suppression to shock — so the nucleus that sets 'wanting' is not valence-selective, and the amygdala's own split is by representational format instead.
- **[[wiki/concepts/information-sampling-vs-search.md]]** — the same multiplier read as a *sampling* policy, and one of two candidate accounts of why animals buy information they cannot use: value assigned to the predictor itself makes reward cues worth looking at (sign-tracking, value-driven capture, proactive search for **redundant** reward cues), which is position B of `T360` against an uncertainty-resolution account — and it is the mechanism by which an attentional bias becomes maladaptive in a task whose goal lies elsewhere.
- **[[wiki/concepts/intrinsic-motivation-typology.md]]** — where that page's uncertainty and learning-progress quantities go when they are *not* additive bonuses: a partially-predictive cue is approached more than a fully-predictive one and leaves the mesolimbic gain sensitized after the contingency becomes deterministic, so the epistemic quantity enters as a cue-addressed multiplier with its own plasticity rather than as a term on the objective (Robinson & Berridge 2025).
- **[[wiki/concepts/temporal-abstraction-options.md]]** — the multiplier is claimed to attach to *action* representations as well as to cues, which gives an option a pursuit weight not derived from its termination value — a persistence mechanism, and a failure mode (an option run for its own sake), that no option framework in the wiki can express.
- **[[wiki/concepts/cognitive-control.md]]** — placed downstream of this page's quantity by the theory's own concession: prefrontal control is what restrains the amplified urge rather than what generates or explains it, so a control failure and a gain excess produce the same behaviour and are separated only by whether the urge is target-specific.
- **[[wiki/entities/lateral-habenula.md]]** — a proposed joint address for this page's two dissociable quantities: dopamine cells signal value *change* ('wanting') and serotonin cells a tonic value *state* (mood, proposed as 'liking'), and the habenula is one of the few structures writing to both — so the node that could couple them computes neither, and its slow burst gain moves both at once. It is also where acute stress is measured doing the opposite of this page's amplification: the same imaged cells' reward response inverts in sign while licking bout duration — a hedonic index — halves, trial-by-trial correlated (`R = −0.24`), so one stressor lowers a 'liking'-class measure through an identified channel (`T362`, `T369`).
